summary.headline: Ashok Leyland Q2 FY27 revenue rose 39% YoY to INR13,364 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.1% (from 12.1%) on steel and commodity inflation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record Q2 domestic CV volumes (59,575 units, +34% YoY) and revenue of INR13,364 crore (+39% YoY), with PAT of INR869 crore (+13%). Material cost rose to 74.9% of revenue from 71.5% in Q1, yet EBITDA margin held at 10.1% through price recovery and mix. Management said margin-percentage tracking should be suspended until commodity costs ease, and flagged discrepancies in Hinduja Leyland Finance (HLF) loan balances, with the auditors issuing a disclaimer of opinion. Net cash surplus widened to INR3,546 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,162 crore in Q2 FY26 (margin 12.1%); margin flat QoQ
positive swing of INR2,556 crore YoY

financial_highlights.value: INR240 crore in Q2; INR393 crore in H1

segments.name: Domestic M&HCV
segments.commentary: Volumes up 44% YoY; market share 32.1%, up 120 bps YoY, with trucks gaining about 150 bps. Multi-axle share of truck volumes rose to about 25% in Q2 from 20% in Q1.

segments.name: Domestic LCV
segments.commentary: Volumes 21,371 units, up 21% YoY; VAHAN market share 13.6%, up 30 bps YoY.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Volumes 5,102 units, up 7% YoY. GCC volumes fell about 20% on West Asia logistics disruption affecting Ras Al Khaimah; SAARC and Africa grew strongly.

segments.name: Aftermarket and Power Solutions
segments.commentary: Domestic aftermarket revenue up 20% YoY; Power Solutions revenue up 33% YoY.

segments.name: Defence (incl. subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 66% YoY to about INR400 crore in the quarter; order book and tender pipeline described as strong.

segments.name: Electric subsidiaries (Switch, OHM)
segments.commentary: Switch delivered 439 e-buses and 732 e-LCVs in H1 with about 2,800 e-bus order book at end-September. OHM operating fleet about 2,100 e-buses; OHM won an order for over 200 e-MaaS cement trucks.

guidance_outlook: Full-year CV industry growth expected in double digits, potentially mid-teens for M&HCV; LCV expected to grow at a similar pace.
GCC exports expected to turn around in Q3 and Q4 as Ras Al Khaimah returns to near full capacity; Q3 export growth expected to be good, Q4 better.
Price increases of about 100-150 bps planned in Q3 and one more likely in Q4; net sale realisation has risen 1-1.25% each quarter and about 2-2.5% since start of year.
Full-year capex guided to INR1,000-1,200 crore against INR393 crore in H1.
Management says commodity inflation will persist into Q3; it expects a large unrealised price pass-on to benefit margins once inflation moderates. Medium-term mid-teens margin goal is retained.
Battery pack plant at Pillaipakkam (about 4 GW initial, expandable to 8-12 GW) to start production in Q3 of next year; cell manufacturing decision possibly next fiscal.
HLF-NDL merger legal completion expected by end-December; overall process expected to complete within Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation close to 90% in Q2; near-term debottlenecking planned with limited capex, plus a greenfield plant for the next growth phase.
Network at 2,175 touchpoints (1,205 M&HCV, 970 LCV) after 43 added in Q2, focused on north and east.
Battery pack facility near Chennai has all approvals; construction started, production expected in Q3 of next year.
Supplier capacity augmentation for critical components under way.
demand_pricing: Domestic M&HCV industry volumes grew 39% YoY in Q2 and domestic LCV 24%; Ashok Leyland M&HCV grew 44%. October numbers were strong despite a higher base.
ICV trucks led growth, followed by heavy-duty trailers, tippers and multi-axle vehicles; buses grew 22%, the lowest segment.
Management attributes demand to fleet ageing, BS6 TCO advantage, and the GST rationalisation trigger from September-October last year.
Freight costs per vehicle moved up over 50% in the past year; company conceded freight increases to transporters.

No discounting: management says net sale realisation is the only metric tracked. Premiumisation via HIPPO and TAURUS 320/360 HP products and air-suspension MAV launches (up to 4 tonnes extra payload).
Management said NBFC credit supply to CVs is strong and asset-quality stress is limited to one or two NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CV growth outlook for the year, and how are GCC export and pent-up demand shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects double-digit full-year CV growth, possibly mid-teens for M&HCV, with LCV similar. GCC volumes fell about 20% in Q2 but are expected to recover in Q3-Q4 after Ras Al Khaimah supply normalised.

qa_highlights.question: How will profitability evolve as steel prices stay elevated and pass-through lags?
qa_highlights.answer: Management asked analysts to stop judging margin as a percentage of revenue and to look at absolute profit YoY until commodity costs ease. Q3 is expected to remain inflation-hit; a large unrealised price pass-on should benefit margins when inflation moderates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the HLF loan-balance discrepancies and their impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Discrepancies are in loan balances across underlying systems; the impact cannot be ascertained yet, and management expects four to six weeks for review. A system audit is under way and an independent agency is being appointed. The auditors gave a disclaimer of opinion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the HLF-NDL legal and accounting merger, and the Hinduja Housing investment?
qa_highlights.answer: NDL is accounting acquirer with 1 April 2026 as appointed date and adopted the merger in its Q2 results. Legal steps (NBFC licence, ROC filing) are expected by end-December. The separate INR500 crore Hinduja Housing investment will happen at an appropriate time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the electrification and battery strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Battery pack plant starts production in Q3 of next year, initially 4 GW for captive use and expandable to 8-12 GW. Cell manufacturing decision may come next fiscal year. LCVs and buses will electrify first, with M&HCV slower.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 20% QoQ, and what drove LCV share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses are partly variable (plant overheads, logistics, warranty, which is provided upfront for six years). Fixed costs are giving operating leverage. LCV gains came from the Northeast and Central expansion, Saathi and Dost/Bada Dost upgrades; LCV share is 55-60% of addressable market, with new platforms expected to lift it.

risks_watch: HLF loan-balance discrepancies: auditors issued a disclaimer of opinion; impact not yet quantified and HLF's figures carry an unresolved review. Consolidated HLF plus HHFL book value is INR8,313 crore with PAT of INR174 crore in Q2.
Commodity inflation (steel, natural rubber, fuel) with price pass-on lag; Q3 expected to remain a tough inflation quarter.
West Asia logistics disruption and GCC volume recovery timing.
Interest-rate hikes possibly ahead; management says the impact on CV demand over the next two quarters should be limited.
Other expenses and warranty provisioning (six-year warranty) growing faster than volume is a watch item.
Q3 price hike execution and whether the margin recovers as management expects.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and market share, citing record volumes and October strength, but cautious on margins, with management asking investors to focus on absolute profit growth rather than margin percentage. Evasive on the HLF discrepancy, deferring quantification until the independent review completes in four to six weeks.
key_quotes: Material cost as a percentage of revenue increased to 74.9% compared with 71.5% in Q1 of this year, an increase of 340 basis points quarter-on-quarter.
we should temporarily stop looking at the margins in terms of percentage of revenue.
I think we will need about four to six weeks. The Board has decided to initiate a system audit, which is in place.
we remain confident in our ability to create sustainable long-term value for all our shareholders.
